name.text: Selecting clinical trial groups and quality-control samples using combinations

questiontext.text:
(a) A doctor selects \({@pr1@}\) patients from a group of \({@pn1@}\) volunteers to test a new vitamin. How many different groups can be formed?

Number of groups = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) A factory inspector picks \({@pr2@}\) smartphones at random from a box of \({@pn2@}\) to check for defects. How many different samples can the inspector choose?

Number of samples = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Because the order in which items are chosen does not create a different group or sample, use the combination formula:

\(\displaystyle {}_nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}\)

Part (a): Selecting \({@pr1@}\) patients from \({@pn1@}\) volunteers
All selected patients receive the same vitamin, so order does not matter. Substitute \(n = {@pn1@}\) and \(r = {@pr1@}\), simplify \(({@pn1@} - {@pr1@})! = {@rem1@}!\), and cancel \({@rem1@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,({@pn1@} - {@pr1@})!} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,{@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_factors@} \times {@rem1@}!}{({@den1_factors@}) \times {@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_factors@}}{{@den1_factors@}} = \frac{{@num1_prod@}}{{@den1_prod@}} = {@ta1@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of groups} = {@ta1@} }\)

Part (b): Picking \({@pr2@}\) smartphones from a box of \({@pn2@}\)
Picking smartphones A, B, C is the same sample as picking C, B, A, so order does not matter. Substitute \(n = {@pn2@}\) and \(r = {@pr2@}\), simplify \(({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})! = {@rem2@}!\), and cancel \({@rem2@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})!} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@} \times {@rem2@}!}{({@den2_factors@}) \times {@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@}}{{@den2_factors@}} = \frac{{@num2_prod@}}{{@den2_prod@}} = {@ta2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of samples} = {@ta2@} }\)
